customer_question: Our module is registered as a Controller Subsystem, and we want to combine it with a separately Component-registered Host stack to register our End Product. Is this just a combination registration, or is there a different procedure? Also, does it matter that the Host stack's Component registration includes some controller-level content too?
question_variants: Can we directly combine a Controller Subsystem and a Component Host stack into an End Product registration?
Does overlapping LL/RF PHY content in the Host stack's Component registration cause a problem?
Is RF testing exempted with this approach, and do we need profile testing?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to register an End Product by combining their module's existing Controller Subsystem registration with a separately Component-registered Host stack, and was concerned that the Host stack's Component registration -- which included lower-layer content (LL, RF PHY) in addition to the GATT stack -- might conflict with the module's own Controller Subsystem layers.
plain_english_explanation: You can't just directly combine a chip-level certification and a separately-registered software-stack certification into a finished-product certification -- there's a specific registration step for that. During that step, you build a new registration that references both pieces together, and importantly, you get to choose which specific layers from each referenced piece actually apply, so if the software-stack's certification happens to also cover some lower-level radio functionality that overlaps with what your own chip already covers, you can simply leave that overlapping part out without it causing any conflict.
consultant_answer: A Controller Subsystem and a Component-registered Host stack cannot be combined directly into an End Product registration. Instead, performing a new Host Subsystem design registration that references the Component-registered Host stack together with the module's Controller Subsystem produces a registration with equivalent legal effect to an End Product registration. Under this approach, RF testing is exempted, and profile testing is required only if a Bluetooth SIG-defined profile is implemented at the upper layer. Regarding the overlap concern: the layers included in a Component registration can be selectively included or excluded during the design registration process that references it, so any unneeded LL or RF PHY content bundled into the Host stack's Component registration is simply excluded during the Host Subsystem design registration and does not cause a problem.
decision_logic: Combining a module's Controller Subsystem with a separately Component-registered Host stack requires performing a new Host Subsystem design registration that references both (not a direct End Product registration), and any layer overlap between the two references (such as LL/RF PHY content bundled into the Host stack's Component registration) is resolved through selective layer inclusion/exclusion during that design registration process, rather than being a blocking conflict.
final_recommendation: When a customer wants to combine a module's Controller Subsystem with a separately Component-registered Host stack, guide them through a new Host Subsystem design registration referencing both, exempting RF testing and requiring profile testing only for SIG-defined profiles, and reassure them that any overlapping lower-layer content in the Host stack's Component registration can simply be excluded during that process.
risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting a direct End Product registration from a Controller Subsystem and Component-registered Host stack, without going through the correct Host Subsystem design registration process, would not produce a valid registration, and failing to selectively exclude overlapping layer content could create unnecessary inter-layer complications.
